# **Alibi \- Requirements Document**

> Status: this document describes the product as built. Items not yet built are marked **(planned)**. The task-level checklist is in `development_phases_and_todo_list.md`.

# **1\. Product Overview**

The game is an interactive, AI-driven detective mystery game where players are presented with a murder or crime scenario. The player must read the case file and the suspect testimonies, then spend in-game tokens to interrogate AI-powered suspects by text. The AI characters act on their assigned personas and stories, dropping clues but never answering direct accusations outright. Players use their deduction skills, their chat history, their own detective's notes and (at a cost) progressive hints to name the culprit. A correct accusation earns trophies and a wrong one loses trophies. Admins create and publish the cases and tune the game economy from an admin panel.

# **2\. Functional Requirements (FR)**

## **FR1: Game Story and Setup Module**

* **FR1.1:** The system shall display the main scenario (the murder/crime story) to the user at the start of the game, together with the case's scene images.  
* **FR1.2:** The system shall display the initial testimonies of all suspects/witnesses involved in the case on the suspect cards (and in a tooltip when hovering the portrait).  
* **FR1.3:** The system shall allow the user to select any available character to start an interrogation.  
* **FR1.4:** Starting a case shall take the Active Case Lock; the lock is idempotent for the same case and refused (400) while another case is unfinished. The dashboard shows the locked case as Continue and all others as Locked (redacted, CLASSIFIED stamp, no button).  
* **FR1.5:** The identity of the culprit shall never be sent to the client before the case is resolved.

## **FR2: AI Character Interrogation Module**

* **FR2.1:** Each suspect shall be powered by a Large Language Model (LLM) with a prompt detailing their persona, public alibi, hidden truth, confession triggers and the public facts of the other suspects (never their secrets).  
* **FR2.2:** The AI character shall respond to user questions contextually based on their specific persona, and shall remember the last 6 exchanges of the current play-through.  
* **FR2.3:** The AI character shall *not* reveal direct answers to direct accusations (e.g., "Did you kill him?") unless it aligns with a predefined confession state. The confession is gated **on the server**: each suspect has confession keywords; until the question (or one of the last 6) matches, the prompt contains no hidden truth, no confession triggers and no culprit flag, and every suspect gets the same neutral "you are hiding something" line, so guilty and innocent suspects look alike and a successful prompt extraction reveals nothing.  
* **FR2.4:** The AI character shall provide subtle clues or misdirections based on the user's line of questioning.  
* **FR2.5:** Interrogation is text-to-text only: no tools, no web search, no file parsing, output modality `text`; tool calls, images or audio in a reply are discarded.  
* **FR2.6:** Each case has its own LLM model (default `google/gemma-4-31b-it`), chosen by an admin from a list of text-only models within a price cap.

## **FR3: Economy & Token System**

* **FR3.1:** The user shall be allocated 10 tokens on signup (when the OTP is verified), and refilled to the daily allowance every day.  
* **FR3.2:** The system shall deduct 1 token for every question asked, **before** the LLM is called and after moderation and a cheap balance check. The deduction is atomic (Redis DECR, mirrored to PostgreSQL).  
* **FR3.3:** The system shall display the remaining token balance prominently and update it instantly when a question is sent.  
* **FR3.4:** The system shall prevent the user from asking further questions when their token balance reaches zero (input disabled with "Out of tokens. Make your final deduction.").  
* **FR3.5:** A token is refunded when the model fails before producing any answer (timeout, upstream error), at most a configured number of times per player per day. A blocked (moderated) question never costs a token.  
* **FR3.6:** A player never holds more than 10 tokens; winning a case awards trophies only, never tokens.  
* **FR3.7:** An admin can give 1-10 tokens to one player (capped at the 10 a player can hold).

## **FR4: Chat History, Notes and Hints**

* **FR4.1:** The system shall maintain a persistent log of all messages exchanged between the user and every AI character, scoped to the current play-through (a replayed case starts with a blank conversation).  
* **FR4.2:** The user shall be able to view their chat history with any character at any time, on the case page, in a global interrogation log that can be filtered by suspect.  
* **FR4.3:** **Detective's notes.** The player can write notes saved to their account (max 1000 characters, max 200 per case). A note is about one suspect or the case in general, and can be attached to a specific log entry, in which case it quotes the question. Notes appear in the same stream as the logs, under the matching filter.  
* **FR4.4:** **Progressive hints.** An admin can write up to 3 hints per case, easiest first. A player reveals them one at a time; hint *n* costs *n* trophies (1, 3, 6 in total), taken off the reward only if the case is solved. Unrevealed hints are never sent to the client.

## **FR5: Case Resolution**

* **FR5.1:** The system shall provide a mechanism for the user to submit their final accusation by choosing a suspect avatar and confirming it ("Submit Deduction"). Only the player holding the case lock can accuse. **(Entering a motive is planned; the current accusation is the culprit only.)**  
* **FR5.2:** The system shall evaluate the submission on the server, reveal the true outcome (culprit and the case's resolution text) and stamp the case file (SOLVED / GUILTY / WRONG) with a win/loss reveal screen.  
* **FR5.3:** A correct accusation adds the case's reward trophies minus the hint penalty. A wrong one subtracts the case's penalty trophies; trophies never go below zero. The Active Case Lock is released and the closed case can be shown again after a reload.

## **FR6: Admin Panel**

* **FR6.1:** Users have a role (`user` or `admin`). Every `/api/admin/*` route checks the role in the token and again in the database, so a demotion applies at once. Admins log in to `/admin/dashboard`.  
* **FR6.2:** **Global settings:** daily token allowance (1-10), reset time (HH:MM) and IANA time zone, applied to all players without a restart.  
* **FR6.3:** **Case management:** create, edit, publish/unpublish and delete cases (title, synopsis, difficulty, reward and penalty trophies, main plot, resolution, up to 3 hints, LLM model, thumbnail, background music track). New cases are drafts; publishing needs at least 2 suspects and exactly one culprit; cases that have been played cannot be deleted, only unpublished.  
* **FR6.4:** **Suspects and scenes:** manage suspects (avatar, testimony, culprit flag, and the AI persona fields: persona, public alibi, hidden truth, confession triggers, confession keywords) and scene images. One culprit per case; secrets need keywords.  
* **FR6.5:** **Image upload:** admin images are re-encoded to WebP, scaled down and stored in object storage; replaced or deleted images are removed from the bucket.  
* **FR6.6:** **Player support:** find a player by username or email and give them tokens (FR3.7).

## **FR7: Presentation, Audio and Atmosphere**

* **FR7.1:** The UI follows a detective "case file" theme (golden-sunset palette, sharp corners): magnifying-glass cursor, gold frames, film grain and vignette, and props such as tape, stamps, redacted text and red string.  
* **FR7.2:** Suspect answers and testimonies are shown in a typewriter font; new answers type out character by character and can be skipped with a click, Enter or Space.  
* **FR7.3:** Sound effects (button click, paper rustle, typewriter keys, stamp) are synthesised in the browser and can be muted.  
* **FR7.4:** Background music: a main theme everywhere and a per-case track (chosen by the admin) while the player is inside a case, with crossfades, an on/off switch and a volume slider remembered per browser.  
* **FR7.5 (planned):** Rank titles (Rookie, Detective, Inspector, Chief) on the leaderboard and avatar; a loading screen ("Searching the archives...") and page transitions.

# **3\. Development Frameworks & Tools**

* **Frontend (Vite, React 19, TypeScript):** shadcn/ui components with the golden-sunset theme, zod + react-hook-form for every form, Remix icons.  
* **Frontend State Management (Zustand):**  lightweight state for the active case context, the single token balance, chat window, suspect filter and UI toggles.  
* **Frontend Data Fetching (React Query / TanStack Query):**  every endpoint is declared once with `createApi` (`src/api/`), which generates the hooks; handles caching, background updating and optimistic updates for chat logs, token balance and dashboard statistics.  
* **Backend Services (Go / Golang):**  high-concurrency backend for API routing, authentication, queue consumption and interrogation logic, with all input validated and all responses and logs going through shared helpers.  
  * **OpenRouter Go SDK:**  answers interrogations through the per-case model, with `data_collection: deny` so providers that log prompts are avoided.  
  * **Ollama Go Client:**  local development and testing only.  
* **Database workflow:** goose migrations and sqlc generated type-safe queries; no hand-written SQL in Go.  
* **Infrastructure:** Docker Compose (one Dockerfile with `api` and `worker` targets), Brevo SMTP for email, Supabase Storage for images (behind a swappable `storage.Provider`).

# **4\. Non-Functional Requirements (NFR)**

## **NFR1: Performance**

* **NFR1.1:** The AI chat responses must be generated and displayed to the user within 2-3 seconds. Measured against `google/gemma-4-31b-it` via OpenRouter: 1.6 to 2.5 s typical, occasionally about 3 s. Achieved with no SDK retries, a 160-token reply cap, a configurable timeout, concurrent lock/history/cache reads, a Redis balance check before any database read and prompts built once per case and suspect so providers can cache the prefix. Streaming is a possible later improvement.  
* **NFR1.2:** The application UI should load initial stories and testimonies within 2 seconds.

## **NFR2: Security**

* **NFR2.1 (Prompt Injection Prevention):** The AI models must be secured against prompt injection so that users cannot force the AI to break character or reveal the system prompt/solution. Defence in depth: input moderation on a normalised copy of the text (accents, look-alike letters, leetspeak and chat-template tokens handled), strikes and a lockout for repeated injections, an output check that replaces replies leaking the hidden truth or the rules, only the questioned suspect's secrets in the prompt, and the server-side confession gate (FR2.3).  
* **NFR2.2:** User data and chat histories must be stored securely, preventing users from modifying chat logs or token balances through the client. PostgreSQL is the source of truth for balances (Redis is a cache) and the culprit and unrevealed hints never leave the server.  
* **NFR2.3 (Abuse and cost protection):** The OpenRouter credit is protected by per-address and per-player rate limits, one question in flight per player, a daily per-player call allowance, a global concurrency cap, daily call and token budgets, and a circuit breaker for upstream failures (429 with `Retry-After`, or 503). Accounts are capped per address and OTP limits treat `+tag` and Gmail-dot variants as one mailbox.  
* **NFR2.4 (Auth hardening):** OTP rate limiting per email and per IP, wrong-code cap, HMAC-only code storage, login lockout with exponential backoff, bcrypt concurrency bound, refresh-token rotation (each token works once), deny-by-default auth middleware, and avatar size and decode limits. **(Bot protection with Turnstile/hCaptcha is planned.)**

## **NFR3: Scalability**

* **NFR3.1:** The backend must handle concurrent LLM requests from multiple players without degradation. The API and the email worker scale as separate services; the chat writer runs with configurable concurrency; the daily reset is safe with multiple replicas.

## **NFR4: Usability and UX**

* **NFR4.1:** The chat interface must resemble modern messaging apps: detective messages are modern right-aligned bubbles, suspects reply as typewritten paper on the left, with a "Suspect is thinking..." indicator.  
* **NFR4.2:** The token counter must be clearly visible and update instantly upon message submission (dropping by 1 on send, refunded on error).  
* **NFR4.3:** The game must be responsive on mobile and desktop. **(A full mobile pass is planned.)**

## **NFR5: Reliability and Availability**

* **NFR5.1:** The application should have an uptime of at least 99.9%. Services have health endpoints, healthchecks, restart policies and graceful shutdown.  
* **NFR5.2:** If the LLM service times out or fails, the system must handle it gracefully and refund the token for that request (FR3.5). The model call completes even if the client disconnects, and its answer is stored.  
* **NFR5.3:** Queues are reliable: failed emails and chat events are retried with backoff, then dead-lettered (`queue:email:dlq`, `queue:chat:dlq`); queue depths are logged and an `emailctl` tool can inspect, requeue and purge. Chat writes are idempotent (event id is the document id).  
* **NFR5.4:** The daily token reset heals itself: a startup check and a per-minute check run a missed day, and a lock prevents replicas from overlapping.

# **5\. Technical Implementation: AI Character Engineering**

## **5.1 Single Model Architecture**

The system uses one stateless LLM per case to power all characters of that case. The application swaps the "System Prompt" based on the suspect being interrogated, so one model instance can switch personas without separate models. Cloud inference uses the OpenRouter Go SDK; the Ollama client is for local use only.

## **5.2 Character Personalization**

Characters are defined by system prompts built from the suspect's admin-authored fields, in three sections:

* **Persona and public alibi:** personality, speaking style and relationship to the victim, plus the story they tell.  
* **Cross-character awareness:** the other suspects' public facts only, never their secrets.  
* **Strict rules:** reply length, stay in character, ignore out-of-world concepts, injection defence.

The hidden truth and confession triggers are added only when the confession gate opens (5.4).

## **5.3 Restrictions and Guardrails (Preventing Off-Topic Queries)**

* **In-Prompt Guardrails:** strict rules anchor the character to their timeline and setting and tell them to act confused or deflect on out-of-world topics.  
* **Input Moderation:** `llm.Moderate` checks input before it reaches the model. Off-topic (code, math) and injection attempts get a fixed in-character reply and cost no token. Injections count as strikes, with a lockout. This is a speed bump, not the only defence (NFR2.1).  
* **Output check:** each reply is scanned for leaked secrets (8 words in a row from the hidden truth or triggers, or quoted rules) and replaced with a fixed line.

## **5.4 Deception Mechanics (Hiding the Truth)**

* **Dual-State Prompting:** the culprit's prompt has a "Public Alibi" and a "Hidden Truth".  
* **Conditional Confessions:** the suspect denies direct accusations and only confesses if the question contains specific evidence. This is enforced on the server through confession keywords (groups such as `last+study` must all appear in the question or one of the last 6); until then the prompt contains no hidden truth. A suspect without keywords is never gated.  
* **Engineered Flaws:** the culprit's alibi contains intentional inconsistencies (for example, not knowing the final score of a game they claim to have watched) that a clever player can catch under cross-examination.

# **6\. System Design and Architecture (Microservices & Polyglot Persistence)**

This system design is a **Microservices and Polyglot Persistence Architecture** combining custom requirements with the core game mechanics.

## **6.1 Architecture Components & Technology Stack**

**Services Layer:**

* **Main Server (API Gateway, Auth & Core Game Service):**  
  * **Responsibilities:** email/password signup with OTP verification, login, refresh, logout, profile and avatar, dashboard, case start, briefing, notes, hints, accusation, and the admin API (settings, cases, suspects, scenes, uploads, token grants). Also runs the daily token reset job and the chat-writer goroutines.  
  * **Security & Pre-Flight Checks:** validates JWTs against the **Redis Token Blacklist** on every request, checks the role for admin routes, and checks and deducts question tokens in Redis before routing chat requests.  
* **LLM Interrogation Service (inside the Main Server, package `internal/interrogation` and `internal/llm`):**  
  * **Responsibilities:** moderation, the confession gate, dynamic System Prompt building, the model call, output checking, the token spend and refund, and abuse guards.  
  * **Speed Optimization:** returns the reply directly within 2-3 seconds while asynchronously pushing the exchange to the message queue.  
* **Chat Storage Worker:** consumes `queue:chat:events` and writes to **MongoDB** (`chat_messages`), so database writes never slow the reply. Also serves historical chat logs (`GET /api/chat/{case_id}/{suspect_id}`).  
* **Email Worker (`cmd/worker`):** a separate process that consumes `queue:email:outbound` and sends OTP emails through Brevo SMTP, with retry, DLQ and its own `/health`. Scalable with `--scale email-worker=N`.

**Data & Caching Layer:**

* **Redis (Upstash):**  
  * **JWT Token Blacklist:** `blacklist:jwt:<jti>` with a TTL equal to the token's remaining lifetime.  
  * **Leaderboard:** a ZSET `leaderboard` updated with ZINCRBY on every trophy change and rebuilt from PostgreSQL every 5 minutes (or when empty or after a Redis outage).  
  * **Cache and guards:** question token balances (`user:coins:<id>`), case/suspect/prompt caches, OTP and login rate limits, LLM rate limits and budgets, queues and dead-letter queues, and cron markers.  
* **PostgreSQL (Supabase \- Main Relational DB):**  
  * Users and roles, credentials, trophies and rank index, wallet balances (source of truth), stories, suspects and scenes with the AI persona fields, hints, music tracks, active case locks (with `play_id` and hints used), case results, case notes and global settings (`app_settings`). Schema changes go through goose migrations and sqlc queries.  
* **MongoDB (NoSQL Document DB):**  
  * Stores the high-volume **Chat Histories** (by user, case, suspect and play-through).  
* **Object storage (Supabase Storage, public bucket `alibi-assets`):**  
  * WebP images only (avatars, thumbnails, scenes, suspect portraits) and background music (`music/*.ogg`), behind a swappable `storage.Provider`.  
* **Core Programming Languages, Frameworks & Libraries (React, Zustand, React Query & Go):**  
  * Used as described in section 3.

## **6.3 End-to-End![][image2] Data Flow (Sequence)**

**How the Data Flows Across the Requirements:**

1. **Authentication & Logged-Out Token Blacklist (Main Server \+ Redis \+ PostgreSQL):**  
   1. On signup the server stores a pending signup and queues an OTP email; no PostgreSQL row exists until the code is verified. On verification the user row is created (10 tokens, 0 trophies) and a JWT pair is issued. Login and refresh also issue tokens; refresh tokens rotate.  
   2. When the user logs out, the server writes the access and refresh token IDs (jti) to **Redis** under blacklist:jwt:\<jti\> with an expiry equal to the remaining lifespan.  
   3. On every request the server checks Redis first; a blacklisted token gets 401.  
2. **Daily Question Tokens & Admin Config (Main Server \+ Redis \+ PostgreSQL):**  
   1. New users receive 10 tokens when their OTP is verified. PostgreSQL is the source of truth and **Redis** (user:coins:\<user\_id\>) is the cache used for 1-5 ms pre-flight checks.  
   2. Each day at the admin-configured time and zone, a cron job sets every balance to exactly the daily allowance (no rollover) in PostgreSQL, then drops the Redis keys. The schedule comes from `app_settings` and is re-read every minute.  
3. **AI Suspect Interrogation (Main Server \-\> LLM \-\> External Model):**  
   1. The server verifies the JWT, runs abuse guards and input moderation (a blocked question is free), does a cheap balance check, then atomically spends 1 token in **Redis** (mirrored to PostgreSQL).  
   2. It builds the suspect's System Prompt (applying the confession gate), adds the last 6 exchanges of this play-through, and calls the case's model.  
   3. If the model fails before answering, the token is refunded (within the daily refund cap); an unusable answer keeps the token.  
4. **Asynchronous Chat Persistence (Interrogation \-\> Queue \-\> Chat Worker \-\> MongoDB):**  
   1. The reply goes back to the player immediately.  
   2. The exchange is pushed to `queue:chat:events` (with retries and an in-memory fallback if the queue refuses it).  
   3. The chat worker inserts it into MongoDB, idempotently. The case page reads the history through `GET /api/chat/{case_id}/{suspect_id}`.  
5. **Case Resolution, Trophies & Leaderboard (Main Server \+ PostgreSQL \+ Redis):**  
   1. When the user submits a suspect, the server checks PostgreSQL for the true culprit.  
   2. **Correct Guess:** the reward trophies minus the hint penalty are added in PostgreSQL (no bonus tokens), the lock is released, a case result is stored and the **Redis Leaderboard** is updated with ZINCRBY by the exact change.  
   3. **Wrong Guess:** the penalty trophies are deducted (never below zero) in PostgreSQL and Redis, and the lock is released.  

# **7\. User Journey and Stories**

## **Phase 1: Onboarding and Authentication**

* **User Story 1.1: Account Creation, Login & Avatar Onboarding**  
  * **As a** new player,  
  * **I want to** sign up and log into the game with my email and choose my detective avatar,  
  * **So that** I can securely save my game progress, chat logs, trophies, and token balances across sessions.  
  * **Acceptance Criteria & Technical Details:**  
    * **Signup Options:** Email with a custom Detective Name/Username and password. Or **Continue with Google**, implemented in our own backend (OAuth authorization code flow with PKCE): the first Google sign-in creates the account (no password, generated detective name, 10 starting tokens, then avatar onboarding), a later one signs in, and a Google account whose verified email matches an existing account is linked to it.  
    * **Authentication & OTP Verification:** Custom email/password authentication in the Go backend (not Supabase Auth). Signups are verified with a One-Time Password sent through Brevo SMTP by the email worker, with resend, cooldowns and rate limits.  
    * **Onboarding Avatar Selection:** After verification, users pick a default avatar (1-4) or upload a custom image (max 1 MB, resized to 256x256 WebP).  
    * **Initial Wallet Allocation:** A starting balance of 10 question tokens is allocated when the OTP is verified.  
    * **Secure Logout:** Logging out blacklists the active tokens in Redis so they can never be reused.

## **Phase 2: The Home Page (Case Selection & Leaderboard)**

* **User Story 2.1: Selecting a Mystery & Viewing Dashboard Stats**  
  * **As a** detective (player),  
  * **I want to** view a dashboard of available crime cases, my remaining tokens, my total trophies, and the top players,  
  * **So that** I can track my rank and choose which mystery I want to solve.  
  * **Acceptance Criteria & Technical Details:**  
    * **Story Cards:** Each card displays the title, synopsis, thumbnail, difficulty and the trophy reward.  
    * **Prominent Balances:** The dashboard shows the player's token balance, trophies and solved count.  
    * **Redis-Powered Leaderboard:** A global leaderboard of the top detectives by trophies, read from a Redis sorted set (rebuilt from PostgreSQL every 5 minutes), marking the player's own row.  
    * **Active Case Lock Mechanic:** Once a player starts a case they are locked into it until they submit their accusation. That card shows Continue and the others are Locked. Only published cases are listed.

## **Phase 3: The Story and Briefing Page**

* **User Story 3.1: Reading the Crime Scenario & Testimonies**  
* **As a** detective,  
* **I want to** read the main crime scenario at the start of the game,  
* **So that** I understand the context of the crime, the victim, and the crime scene.  
* **Acceptance Criteria & Technical Details:**  
  * **Story Dashboard:** Selecting a case opens `/case/:id`.  
  * **Plot & Visuals:** A framed scene gallery beside the letter-shaped case file with the main plot.  
  * **Character Avatars:** Suspects are shown in a horizontal carousel with avatar, name, role and initial testimony on the card; hovering the portrait also shows the testimony in a tooltip.  
  * **Chat button:** Each suspect card has a Chat button that opens the floating chat window with that suspect selected.

**User Story 3.2: Initiating Interrogation & Reviewing History**

* **As a** detective,  
* **I want to** select any suspect,  
* **So that** I can enter a chat interface to interrogate them and review past conversations.  
* **Acceptance Criteria & Technical Details:**  
  * **Chat Interface:** The Chat button opens a floating chat window to converse with that AI character.  
  * **Global Chat History:** The case page has an interrogation log section showing the user's exchanges.  
  * **Character-Specific History:** Filter pills, or clicking a suspect card, filter the log to that suspect.  
  * **Chat Previews:** The log shows previews of earlier exchanges before a chat is reopened.

**User Story 3.3: Detective's Notes**

* **As a** detective,  
* **I want to** write notes on the case, on a suspect, or on one answer,  
* **So that** I can keep track of inconsistencies.  
* **Acceptance Criteria:** Notes are saved to my account (FR4.3), shown in the same stream as the logs, filterable by suspect, and can be deleted by their owner only.

**User Story 3.4: Using Hints**

* **As a** stuck detective,  
* **I want to** reveal hints one at a time,  
* **So that** I can make progress at a known cost to my reward.  
* **Acceptance Criteria:** Up to 3 hints per case; hint *n* costs *n* trophies, charged only if I solve the case (FR4.4).

## **Phase 4: The Interrogation (Core Gameplay Loop)**

* **User Story 4.1: Chatting with Suspects & Roleplay**  
* **As a** detective,  
* **I want to** ask questions to an AI-powered suspect and receive contextual, persona-driven responses,  
* **So that** I can gather subtle clues and catch them in lies.  
* **Acceptance Criteria & Technical Details:**  
  * The AI responds within 2-3 seconds, and answers type out in a typewriter effect.  
  * The AI stays strictly in character based on their assigned role.  
  * The AI refuses off-topic queries without charging a token.  
  * The culprit will *never* reveal the truth directly or confess unless the question contains the specific evidence (server-side gate).  
  * **User Story 4.2: Managing the Token Economy & Daily Limits**  
* **As a** detective,  
* **I want to** see my remaining token balance prominently displayed,  
* **So that** I know how many questions I have left.  
* **Acceptance Criteria & Technical Details:**  
  * **Token Cost:** exactly 1 token per question (1 query \= 1 token), spent before the model is called.  
  * **Initial Balance:** 10 tokens on signup.  
  * **Daily Refresh Mechanism:** balances are reset to the daily allowance every day.  
  * **No Rollover:** unused tokens do not roll over (5 left means 10 the next day, not 15).  
  * **Admin Configuration:** the daily allowance (1-10) and the reset time and time zone are configured by an administrator on the admin settings page and apply to all users.  
  * **Refunds:** failures before any answer refund the token (FR3.5).  
  * The visual token counter updates instantly upon message submission.  
  * **User Story 4.3: Hitting the Token Limit**  
* **As a** detective,  
* **I want to** be notified when my token balance reaches zero,  
* **So that** I understand I can no longer interrogate suspects and must make my final deduction.  
* **Acceptance Criteria:** The chat input is disabled with a clear message when tokens run out.  
  * **User Story 4.4: Reviewing Clues**  
* **As a** detective,  
* **I want to** view my persistent chat history with every character at any time,  
* **So that** I can cross-reference their answers and find inconsistencies.  
* **Acceptance Criteria:** The system keeps a persistent log of all messages in the current play-through, and players can switch between characters to review them.

## **Phase 5: Case Resolution**

* **User Story 5.1: Making the Accusation & Trophies System**  
* **As a** detective,  
* **I want to** submit my final deduction by selecting the culprit,  
* **So that** I can find out if I solved the case and earn rewards.  
* **Acceptance Criteria & Technical Details:**  
  * **Accusation Submission:** the user opens the accusation screen, picks a suspect avatar and confirms with "Submit Deduction". Entering a motive is **planned**.  
  * **Rewards (Correct Accusation):** the case's reward trophies minus any hint penalty; winning never awards chat tokens. The leaderboard is updated.  
  * **Penalties (Incorrect Accusation):** the case's penalty trophies are deducted (never below zero), and no tokens are awarded.  
  * **Outcome Reveal:** a win/loss reveal with the culprit, the resolution text and a SOLVED / GUILTY / WRONG stamp on the case file.  
  * **Trophies Display:** trophies are shown on the dashboard next to the token balance.

## **Phase 6: Admin Panel**

* **User Story 6.1: Running the game**  
* **As an** administrator,  
* **I want to** create cases, tune the economy and help players,  
* **So that** the game can grow without code changes.  
* **Acceptance Criteria & Technical Details:** see FR6. Includes the case list with status and readiness, a long-scroll case builder (basic info, thumbnail, case file, resolution, hints, suspect cards with AI persona, scenes, music track, publish) with "Save as draft" and "Save & publish", a searchable AI model dropdown, global settings, and a player token grant.

## **Cross-phase: Presentation and Audio**

* See FR7: theme, typewriter text, synthesised sound effects with a mute toggle, and background music with per-case tracks.

## **Planned / Not Yet Built**

* Bot protection (Turnstile or hCaptcha) on signup and resend-otp.
